songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High-energy Other One > Big Railroad Blues and tight group performance
ai_show_review.blurb: The show features a powerful Other One → Big Railroad Blues suite, with Jerry’s vocals strong throughout and Phil’s snappy bass front‑and‑center. The first set builds solidly into a high‑energy second half highlighted by Jack Straw, Black Peter and an inspired Keith piano.
ai_show_review.review:
The Dead bring their A‑game to San Antonio Civic Auditorium on November 12, 1971, delivering one of the tighter early‑70s outings of the era. The first set rolls out with a crisp Truckin' that sets a buoyant tone, moving through Loser and Sugaree before a spirited Jack Straw that showcases Bob’s confident vocal delivery despite a brief flub. Phil’s bass is front‑and‑center all night, snapping along to every groove while Keith’s piano adds a bright, sparkling layer that cuts through the mix.

The second set erupts with an electrifying Other One → Big Railroad Blues suite that feels both relentless and cohesive; Jerry’s guitar weaves luminous leads as Phil drives a tasty low‑end foundation. Billy’s drumming locks in tightly, propelling the band forward into a rousing Big Railroad Blues that segues seamlessly into a joyous Sugar Magnolia closeout. Overall, the performance is high‑energy, well‑balanced, and captures the band at a moment when each member is locked in and the group chemistry shines.

best_recording.reason: Good overall mix captures the full show with clear instrument separation; despite slight hiss it remains the most complete and reliable soundboard source.

key_highlights: Monster Other One → Big Railroad Blues suite that drives the second set
Snappy, front‑and‑center Phil Lesh bass throughout both sets
Keith Godchaux's upfront piano adds sparkle and uniqueness to the performance
High‑energy group playing with tight rhythm section lock between Billy and Phil

band_performance.Jerry: Vocals are strong all night with only a minor flub on Jack Straw; guitar work is solid and inspirational, especially during the Other One jam.
band_performance.Phil: Bass lines are snappy, front‑and‑center and tastefully tasty, providing a powerful foundation for the improvisations.
band_performance.Bob: Vocals generally praised, anchoring the songs with confidence; rhythm guitar locks tightly with the band despite a brief slip on Jack Straw.
band_performance.Keith: Upfront piano adds sparkle, sounding slightly high in early tracks but remains perfectly played and inspired throughout.
band_performance.Billy: Snappy, driving beat that locks tightly with Phil’s bass, keeping the group tight and propulsive.
